name: ConfigUX 2D & 3D Product Configurator
author: ConfigUX

sections.description:
Help customers see what they are choosing. Build interactive 2D and 3D configurators in ConfigUX Studio, then show them on your WordPress website.

Let buyers explore colours, materials and product options, see updated prices, request a quote or continue to your WooCommerce cart.

  • Visual choices: layered 2D images and interactive 3D models.
  • Live pricing: show the price of the selected configuration.
  • Dimensions: add measurements and resizing for models set up to support them.
  • AR previews: view compatible 3D models in your space on supported mobile devices.
  • Quotes or purchases: use quote requests, optional configuration PDFs and WooCommerce product connections.
  • Your presentation: manage layout, branding, options and price wording in Studio.

The plugin is free. A ConfigUX account and the hosted ConfigUX service are required. Service plans, trials and limits are separate from the plugin. See https://configux.com/ for current plans and demos.

Works with a WordPress Shortcode block or an Elementor Shortcode widget. WooCommerce is optional and remains responsible for products, stock, tax, cart, checkout and orders. Purchase prices are validated server-side before cart handoff.

External services

Connection is an explicit administrator action. Activation does not create a ConfigUX account or automatically pair the website.

The plugin uses these ConfigUX services after connection:

  • https://account.configux.com – ConfigUX sign-in, Studio and website-connection approval.
  • https://api.configux.com – server-side connection and status checks, signed synchronization and API requests for publications, saved configurations, quotes, analytics and price/cart validation. Some connector routes also use account.configux.com.
  • https://player.configux.com – website-bound Player delivery, publication packages and assets.

Refresh retrieves the paired workspace’s published configurator names, publication identifiers and available preview images, plus this website’s saved connections. It does not publish a configurator or insert it into a page.

Connection exchanges website endpoints, connector capabilities and short-lived proofs. Later requests use site/workspace/publication identifiers and signed request metadata. Embedded pages retrieve the publication and required assets.

Save, quote and cart actions send the selected configuration and enabled inputs. Quotes may include contact details, messages, previews and attachments submitted by the buyer. Cart validation sends the connected product, quantity and configuration. Connected WooCommerce sale/refund reports include order/line identifiers, currency and relevant line amounts; they exclude buyer names, contact details, addresses, payment credentials and free text. Unrelated order lines and historical orders are not reported.

ConfigUX terms: https://configux.com/terms/
ConfigUX privacy policy: https://configux.com/privacy-policy/

Privacy

Aggregate configurator statistics count usage and choices without analytics cookies or persistent visitor profiles. Analytics events exclude names, email addresses and free text. Account, quote, saved-configuration, order and security data are processed separately as described in the privacy policy.

This is not a promise that the website or all connected services use no cookies or personal data. Site owners must describe the features they enable and obtain any required consent. Aggregate analytics can be disabled with the configux_cloud_analytics_mode filter.

Disconnect, deactivation, uninstall and cloud-account deletion are separate actions. Retention and deletion follow the applicable ConfigUX service processes and the website owner’s obligations.

Developer information

First-party code is GPL-2.0-or-later. The hosted service and customer content are separate. WordPress.org provides updates for this directory edition; the private updater is excluded.

First-party JavaScript is human-readable. Bundled Google model-viewer is Apache-2.0 with its notices included. Upstream source: https://github.com/google/model-viewer/tree/v4.1.0.
sections.installation:
Use HTTPS and a permalink structure other than Plain.

  1. Install and activate the plugin, then open ConfigUX in WordPress.
  2. Select Connect. Sign in to ConfigUX, check the website and workspace, then select Continue & connect.
  3. Create or open your configurator in Studio and publish it.
  4. In WordPress > ConfigUX, select Refresh to update Your configurators. Select Connect beside a published configurator to choose WordPress, WooCommerce or HTML in Studio. Copy the WordPress shortcode into a Shortcode block or Elementor Shortcode widget.
  5. For purchases, connect the exact WooCommerce product before enabling Add to cart.

If the browser connection cannot complete, use the short-lived connection-code option in WordPress and Studio > Integrations > WordPress + WooCommerce. Do not share connection codes.

Moving from the private ConfigUX Cloud Connector? Back up the site, deactivate the private edition and install this edition. Do not run both together. Deactivation preserves local connection data. Verify the connection and pages before removing the old copy.
sections.faq:
Is WooCommerce required?

No. WordPress pages and quote requests work without WooCommerce. Enable WooCommerce when you want its product, cart and order integration.

Where do I build the configurator?

In ConfigUX Studio. Create choices, connect models or images, set prices and style the layout there. Publish changes when you are ready to update the website.

Can every 3D model resize or open in AR?

No. Dimension-driven resizing requires a model and configuration set up for it. AR requires a compatible model, enabled AR and a supported mobile device/browser.

Is the plugin free?

Yes. The hosted ConfigUX service requires an account and has its own trial, plans and limits. Installing the plugin does not create an account or start a paid subscription.

Can I use the same installation code on another website?

Create an installation for the exact destination in Share & install. Installation codes are restricted to their selected website.

What happens if I deactivate or disconnect?

Deactivation preserves local data for an update or rollback. Disconnect separately revokes the connection. Neither action deletes the ConfigUX account, WordPress products, orders or previously submitted cloud records.
